title: Hosted API: deploy fencing, canary quarantine, and version-pin stabilization
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Problem: Recent partial rollouts have produced short-lived regional surges and hard-to-debug SLO regressions when backend model variants and routing policies diverge. We need an upgrade/hardening set that prevents a single faulty rollout from causing cascade failures across regions or tenant classes. Goal: implement 'fencing' primitives (per-region and per-tenant circuit breakers and surge caps), an automated canary quarantine that halts and isolates misbehaving canaries, and a lightweight version-pin stabilization path for LTS channels so tenants on LTS variants are protected from aggressive auto-rollouts. This ticket covers design, infra changes, integration points with Console SLO dashboards, and rollout automation for the Hosted API pipeline.
acceptance_criteria: Per-region fencing rules implemented and configurable via release policy (max concurrent % of new-version traffic, surge cap absolute)
Automated canary quarantine triggers when error-rate or latency breach exceeds configured band for N consecutive minutes and isolates canary traffic under a quarantine tag
LTS version-pin channel respects pin config and prevents auto-routing changes without explicit opt-in or manual approval
End-to-end e2e test validates that a failing canary does not exceed allowed blast radius (tenant-level and region-level) in CI
Runbook updated and a Console dashboard tile shows active fences/quarantines with links to incident playbook
tasks: Design fencing policy schema and CLI/Console surface (Asha)
Implement runtime fencing hooks in request router (Miguel)
Add quarantine lifecycle state to rollout controller and expose API for forced/unforced quarantine (backend)
Integrate SLO metrics (p95 latency, 5xx rate) as quarantine triggers via telemetry pipeline (observability)
Add unit and integration tests; add e2e scenario in canary CI matrix
Create Console UX to view/override fences and quarantine decisions
Author runbook, KB and update changelog
decisions: Use conservative default: per-region max 10% of traffic for new version, absolute max 200 requests/sec per region until passed gating
Quarantine triggers derived from composite signal: (5xx-rate > 0.5% AND p95 latency increase > 30%) sustained for 3 minutes
LTS channel will be opt-out for enterprises; auto-rollout disabled by default and requires explicit approval or a scheduled maintenance window
Fencing implemented in router layer to minimize blast radius before reaching runtime stacks
Telemetry for quarantine will rely on existing Kinesis metrics + a short-lived aggregated view to avoid long joins
risks: False positives: overly-sensitive quarantine may slow safe rollouts — mitigated by conservative defaults and early canary-bypass flag for staging
Operational complexity: more states in rollout controller increases debugging surface — mitigated by adding clear logging and Console state views
Performance overhead: runtime hooks may add latency — mitigate with fast-path checks and in-memory rate trackers
Coordination with Dedicated/Private: ensure gates are configurable and disabled if customers manage routing locally
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (design + prototype): implement policy schema, runtime hook prototype behind feature flag in staging (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (operator tooling + observability): add Console views, alerts, and QA e2e tests; integrate SLOs (2 weeks)
Phase 3 (canary): enable for 5% of low-risk traffic across 2 regions; monitor for 48h
Phase 4 (regional expansion): gradually open to 25% then 50% with automatic quarantine enabled
Phase 5 (LTS channel enablement): apply version-pin behavior to LTS customers and run migration playbook
Rollback criteria: manual or automatic rollback if quarantine rate > 10% of canaries or if sustained customer-impacting errors observed
